topic.name: The Nth Term of a Geometric Sequence

question.text: Find the formula for the $n$th term of the following geometric sequence. \[ 10, \: -4, \: \dfrac 8 5, \: \ldots \]
question.explanation:
The first term of the sequence is $a_1 = 10$ and the second term is $a_2 = -4,$ so we can find the common ratio, as follows:

\begin{align*} r &= \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} = \dfrac{-4}{10} = -\dfrac{2}{5} \end{align*}

Now that we know the common ratio is $r = -\dfrac{2}{5},$ we can complete the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

\begin{align*} a_n &= a_1 \cdot r^{n-1} \\[5pt] &= 10 \cdot \left( -\dfrac{2}{5} \right)^{n - 1} \end{align*}

example.title: Finding a Formula for the Nth Term of a Geometric Sequence

question.text: Find the formula for the $n$th term of the following geometric sequence. \[ \dfrac 23, \: 3, \: \dfrac{27}{2}, \: \ldots \]
question.explanation:
The first term of the sequence is $a_1 = \dfrac{2}{3}$ and the second term is $a_2 = 3,$ so we can find the common ratio, as follows:

\begin{align*} r &= \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} = \dfrac{3}{\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)} = \dfrac{9}{2} \end{align*}

Now that we know the common ratio is $r = \dfrac 92,$ we can complete the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

\begin{align*} a_n &= a_1 \cdot r^{n-1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{3} \cdot \left( \dfrac 92 \right)^{n - 1} \end{align*}

example.title: Finding a Formula for the Nth Term of a Geometric Sequence

question.text: The first term of a geometric sequence is $1,$ and the common ratio is $-2.$ The $6$th term of this sequence is
question.explanation:
The first term is $a_1=1,$ and the common ratio is $r=-2,$ so we can write the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

\begin{align*} a_n &= a_1 \cdot r^{n-1} \\[5pt] &= 1 \cdot (-2)^{n-1} \end{align*}

To find the $6$th term, we can use this formula with $n=6\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} a_n &= 1 \cdot (-2)^{n-1} \\[5pt] a_{6} &= 1 \cdot (-2)^{6-1} \\[5pt] &= 1 \cdot (-2)^5 \\[5pt] &= 1 \cdot (-32) \\[5pt] &= -32 \end{align*}

Therefore, the $6$th term is $a_{6}=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-32}.$
